canonical_statement: SURMOUNT-1 evaluated the efficacy and safety of once-weekly tirzepatide in adults with obesity or overweight and at least one weight-related complication who did not have diabetes.
Eligible participants were adults with BMI at least 30 kg/m², or BMI at least 27 kg/m² plus at least one weight-related complication, with at least one unsuccessful dietary effort to lose weight.

canonical_statement: The phase 3 trial was multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, and conducted at 119 sites in nine countries.
Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1:1:1 ratio to tirzepatide 5 mg, 10 mg, 15 mg, or placebo, with randomization stratified by country, sex, and prediabetes status.
Tirzepatide was started at 2.5 mg once weekly and increased by 2.5 mg every 4 weeks during a 20-week dose-escalation period to the assigned maintenance dose of 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg.
The comparator was matching once-weekly placebo administered with the same lifestyle intervention.

exposures.details: Given with the same lifestyle intervention

canonical_statement: All treatment groups received lifestyle counseling targeting an approximately 500-kcal/day energy deficit and at least 150 minutes of physical activity per week.

exposures.details: Counseling for an approximately 500-kcal/day energy deficit and at least 150 minutes/week of physical activity

canonical_statement: One coprimary end point was percent change in body weight from baseline to week 72.

concept.text: Percent change in body weight from baseline

canonical_statement: The other coprimary end point was the proportion of participants with at least 5% body-weight reduction at week 72.
The treatment-regimen estimand assessed the treatment effect at week 72 regardless of adherence to the assigned intervention or discontinuation.
The efficacy estimand addressed a hypothetical effect if participants had remained on the randomized treatment through week 72.

For the treatment-regimen estimand, continuous outcomes used multiple imputation followed by ANCOVA and binary outcomes used logistic regression; missing data after non-COVID intercurrent events were imputed from retrieved dropouts in the same treatment group.
For the efficacy estimand, repeated continuous measures were analyzed using a mixed model for repeated measures under a missing-at-random assumption, with imputation-derived binary outcomes.

The final protocol amendment (b), approved October 4, 2021, updated key secondary objectives and end points and aligned analyses with the updated statistical analysis plan while the trial was ongoing.

The final statistical analysis plan was version 2, approved September 28, 2021; revisions included detailed type I error control, updates to multiple imputation following FDA comments, and changes to selected key secondary end points.
Trial masking included participants, investigators, site personnel, and study monitors; an independent data monitoring committee reviewed unblinded safety analyses.

canonical_statement: Gastrointestinal adverse events were reported as mostly mild to moderate in severity and occurred most often during the dose-escalation period.
The authors noted that trial volunteers may represent a subpopulation with greater commitment to weight-management efforts than the broader eligible population.
Only 5.5% of participants had BMI 27 to less than 30 kg/m², limiting inference for the overweight-with-comorbidity subgroup.
The authors stated that longer-term studies are needed to determine durability and longer-term effects beyond the 72-week primary trial period.
The authors concluded that 72 weeks of once-weekly tirzepatide at 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg provided substantial and sustained reductions in body weight in adults with obesity.
The trial was funded by Eli Lilly.

Eli Lilly designed and oversaw the conduct of the trial, monitored sites, collated and analyzed data, and provided medical-writing and editorial assistance through an employee; investigators collected data and the authors interpreted results and vouched for trial fidelity.
